chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Muawiya ibn Wahb who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saw me while I was carrying vegetables, so he said: 'It is disliked for a man of magnanimity to carry a lowly thing, lest people become audacious (disrespectful) toward him.'

key_terms.الدَّنِيّ: Lowly, base, or demeaning — something socially beneath one's station
key_terms.السَّرِيّ: A man of nobility, magnanimity, or high social standing; one whose dignity is recognizable to others
key_terms.يُجْتَرَأَ عَلَيْهِ: To be bold/audacious toward someone; to lose one's respectful restraint in dealings with them
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: Makruh — religiously disliked or discouraged, a legal category below haram (forbidden)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about a noble man carrying lowly things in public?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) observed his companion Muawiya ibn Wahb carrying vegetables and used the occasion to teach about social dignity. He ruled that it is makruh (religiously disliked) for a noble or respected man to carry degrading items in public, because such behavior could lead people to lose their respect for him. This teaching reflects the broader Islamic concern for maintaining the dignity of religious leadership and social standing in community life.
